title: Jharkhand wage delays and incomplete works shadow MGNREGS record
dek: An audit of MGNREGS in Jharkhand shows wage arrears of over 321 crore rupees and a quarter of planned works never started, while the official record cannot confirm what workers actually received.
theme: Wage arrears and incomplete works in Jharkhand's MGNREGS
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in Jharkhand was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: In Jharkhand, rural families depend on MGNREGS for their daily income, and the scheme assures work within a set timeframe. According to the audit, the state government's fund releases for the scheme were delayed by 40 to 55 days, which the audit says undermined the goal of offering work to those needing daily wages. The report does not mention the number of households impacted by these delays or how they reacted.

The audit also noted that as of March 2025, unpaid wages for unskilled workers from 2019-20 to 2023-24 totalled 321.84 crore rupees. It says that failing to pay wages denied workers their rightful earnings and created financial strain, but it does not give individual examples of such hardship. The report does not specify how many workers were affected or the waiting period for each.

For the years 2019-24, the audit looked at 1,02,68,484 planned works. It found that only 27 per cent were finished, 49 per cent remained unfinished as of March 2024, and 24 per cent were never started. Spending on these works reached 2,633 crore rupees, but the report does not indicate how much of that money led to usable assets. The audit does not tie the unfinished works to specific wage delays, nor does it explain why they were not completed.

section.title: What the record shows about works

body.text: In six test-checked districts, the audit scrutinised 480 works and found 139 lying incomplete as of January 2025. The audit also found that mandatory records like Measurement Books and Muster Rolls were not maintained, and that the NREGASoft portal lacked controls to prevent payments without validated data. The record shows cases of payments released even when measurements were not recorded or were incomplete, but it does not quantify how many such payments occurred across the state.

The audit identified mismatches between NREGASoft portal data and the department's certified financial accounts. In three test-checked districts, 32.62 lakh rupees were spent improperly on items like maintaining old vehicles and paying salaries for functionaries not covered by the scheme. The report does not state whether these were isolated cases or part of a broader issue, and it does not name the districts.

The audit further states that the State Employment Guarantee Council did not hold monitoring or steering meetings on a regular basis, and that staffing shortages ranged from 8.24 to 21.07 per cent. The report does not explain why the council failed to meet regularly or how the staffing gaps affected wage disbursements. It also does not directly link these monitoring lapses to the unpaid wages, leaving that connection unexamined.

perspectives.label: Audit
perspectives.rationale: The audit is an independent examination of the institution's own records, and it can contradict or narrow the institution's account.
perspectives.sees: The audit sees discrepancies between portal data and financial accounts, and it sees wage arrears and incomplete works.
perspectives.values: The audit values accuracy in records and adherence to scheme rules.
perspectives.uses: The audit uses official records and physical verification to support its findings.
perspectives.mayMiss: The audit may miss the lived experience of workers and the reasons behind delays.

perspectives.label: Workers
perspectives.rationale: Workers are the intended beneficiaries of the scheme, and their perspective is not directly represented in the audit record.
perspectives.sees: Workers would see the impact of wage delays on their daily lives.
perspectives.values: Workers value timely wages and reliable employment.
perspectives.uses: Workers use the scheme as a source of income.
perspectives.mayMiss: Workers may miss the systemic reasons for delays and the broader audit findings.
